why.text: Native grapes grow on volcanic ash behind stone walls, coping with wind and 150 mm of rain. The wines are balanced and mineral.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines, with or without oak; also liqueur, sparkling and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Very little rain (150 mm) and wind; vines are shielded by low stone walls.

tastes.text: Whites: straw to greenish yellow. Rosés and reds: red in every shade. Frank fruity and floral aromas of medium intensity; fresh, balanced, persistent. Barrel-aged: vanilla, spice, balsamic, toast.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Ripe, raisined, candied fruit; dense, tasty, balanced and very complex.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Fine constant bubbles; fresh fruit, white flowers, bakery notes; fine and elegant.

why.text: Native grapes grow on volcanic soil under an Atlantic climate with trade winds. Days and nights swing widely, and rain is scarce but sufficient.

styles.text: White, rosado, claret and red wines, plus Tea wines, liqueur, sparkling, needle and sweet wines.

climate.text: Atlantic, with trade winds; wide swings in temperature over the year and between day and night; scarce but sufficient rain.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow in all shades. Rosés and reds: red in all shades. Clean aromas of the variety; fresh, tasty, balanced. Tea and aged wines show the aromas and flavours of their maturation.

styles.name: Vino de Tea
styles.text: Must show the aromas and flavours of its maturation.

styles.name: Malvasía dulce
styles.text: Late-harvest overripe grapes; golden yellow, unctuous, intense aroma.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Traditional method, white varieties; yellow, unctuous, raisins and spice, velvety.

styles.name: Vino de aguja
styles.text: Traditional method; fine bubbles, medium to high intensity, tasty and balanced.

why.text: A long growing season ripens grapes slowly on clay-loam and silt-loam soil. The wines are intense and aromatic.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines; also liqueur, sparkling, sweet and naturally sweet wines.

climate.text: Long vegetative period and slow ripening.

tastes.text: Reds: cherry to deep garnet; fruity, herbal, mineral; good structure, quality tannin. Whites: steely to greenish yellow; fruity, floral, balsamic. Rosés: strawberry to onion-skin; fruity, fresh.

styles.name: Vino naturalmente dulce
styles.text: Ripe, even raisined grape notes; balance and harmony on the palate.

styles.name: Vino de uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: Ripe, even raisined grape notes; sweetness and acidity in balance.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Ripe-grape and raisin notes; alcohol, sweetness and acidity in balance.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Small constant bubbles; clean, fruity, varietal; lively, broad fruity finish.

why.text: Vines climb from 300 to 1,700 m in a sunny basin in south-east Tenerife. Porous volcanic soil lies low down, with fertile clay higher up.

styles.text: Dry and off-dry whites, rosado and reds; liqueur wines, classic sweet wines and needle wines.

climate.text: Rain from 161 mm to 504 mm at Izaña a year; very high sunshine, the most sun hours in Spain.

soil.text: Porous volcanic soils at 400 to 800 m; dark, fertile clay soils at 800 to 1,700 m.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to straw; fruit and floral notes, hints of fresh herb or balsam; tasty, fresh, fruity finish. Reds: cherry to garnet; ripe fruit, earthy and spicy touches. Rosés: pink, red fruit.

styles.name: Vino dulce clásico
styles.text: Pale yellow to straw; fruit, honeyed and balsamic notes; tasty to powerful.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Golden to amber, or cherry to garnet; candied fruit, toasted, honeyed; sweet.

styles.name: Espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Pale yellow to gold, fine bubbles, persistent crown, fruity with bakery hints.

why.text: Vines grow on gentle slopes at 400 to 800 m, mostly on volcanic soil. Temperatures are mild.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines; also liqueur, sparkling and classic sweet wines.

climate.text: Mild: summer high 37 °C, winter low 7 °C; about 2,000 sun hours and 465 mm of rain a year.

soil.text: About 70% volcanic soil, 20% clay and 10% volcanic rock.

altitude.text: Vineyards on gentle slopes at 400 to 800 m.

tastes.text: Reds: red with violet glints to tile; red fruit, pepper, balsamic; balanced. Whites: greenish yellow to amber; floral, anise and fennel; fresh. Rosés: cherry pink to onion-skin; fruity, fresh.

styles.name: Tinto de maceración
styles.text: Picota red to purple, soft on the palate.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Candied fruit, toasted and honeyed notes; balanced, intense, fruity finish.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Fine bubbles, persistent crown; finer aromas than plain sparkling wine.

styles.name: Vino espumoso aromático de calidad
styles.text: Fine bubbles, persistent crown; great aromatic intensity.

why.text: Slopes fall from Teide to the coast, from 1,400 to 50 m, on fertile volcanic soil. The vines get trade winds and strong sun.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines; also liqueur, sparkling and sweet Malvasía wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Shaped by altitude, trade winds, the Atlantic current and strong sunshine.

soil.text: Volcanic; sandy-loam or loam, acid, fertile, low in sodium and potassium.

altitude.text: Vineyards from 1,400 m down to 50 m.

tastes.text: Whites: yellow with green or amber tones; fresh, balanced, fruity finish. Reds: violet-tinged picota red; red fruit, medium tannin; aged ones show ripe fruit, vanilla, toast. Rosés: pink, moderate body.

styles.name: Malvasía Clásico
styles.text: Overripe-grape wine, yellow, unctuous; raisins, spice, dried apricot; velvety.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Yellow, pink or ruby, unctuous; raisins and spice; velvety, intense.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: Pale yellow to gold, small persistent bubbles; clean, fruity, fresh.

why.text: Vines grow from 300 to 1,700 m on gentle slopes in arid south-east Tenerife. The heat is high and the sun strong.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds; also sparkling, needle, liqueur and classic sweet wines.

climate.text: Harsh: very arid, high temperatures and strong sunshine, with low rainfall.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to golden straw; tropical fruit, floral, balsamic; fresh, balanced, slightly acid. Reds: cherry with violet tones; red fruit, vegetal, mineral. Rosés: pale to deep pink; red fruit.

styles.name: Vino dulce clásico
styles.text: Candied fruit, honeyed, nut notes; powerful, tasty, glyceric, persistent.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Golden to amber, or cherry to garnet; candied fruit, toasted, honeyed.

styles.name: Aguja gasificado
styles.text: Fine bubbles; fruity and floral; broad, peppery, slightly acid.

why.text: The island has many microclimates and steep terraces. Forastera Blanca, the majority white grape, gives high, balanced acidity.

styles.text: Whites (including single-variety Forastera), rosados, reds (some carbonic maceration), liqueur, sparkling and sweet wines.

tastes.text: Reds: picota red with violet tones; red fruit or floral; balanced, moderately tannic. Whites: greenish yellow to amber; fresh, balanced, fruity finish. Rosés: raspberry to onion-skin.

styles.name: Tinto de maceración carbónica
styles.text: Banana aroma predominates; short on the palate.

styles.name: Blanco monovarietal Forastera
styles.text: Single-variety white, greenish yellow to amber; fresh, balanced, fruity finish.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Yellow, unctuous; raisins and spice; velvety, intense, fruity finish.

styles.name: Vino naturalmente dulce
styles.text: Overripe-grape wine, yellow, unctuous; raisins and spice; velvety.

why.text: Geography and soils vary widely, with trade winds and warmth from the African coast. The wines are structured and balanced.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines; also liqueur, sparkling and classic sweet wines.

climate.text: Trade winds and warmth from the African coasts.

tastes.text: Reds: garnet, cherry or ruby; red fruit, pepper, tobacco, dark chocolate; clove and vanilla when aged. Whites: pale straw, green rims; tropical fruit, apple, citrus, fennel, anise. Structured, broad, persistent.

styles.name: Dulce clásico
styles.text: Pale yellow to gold; ripe or raisined white fruit, honeyed; sweet, unctuous.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Raisined and overripe fruit, tropical, citrus, nuts, mineral; balanced, persistent.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Pale yellow, fine bubbles; fresh, fruity and floral aromas.

why.text: Steep terraces run from 50 to 1,000 m on loose, stony soil with low rainfall. The wines are high in alcohol and acidity.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines; also liqueur, sparkling and classic sweet wines.

climate.text: Low rainfall; the document calls the island's climate and soils unique.

altitude.text: Vineyards between 50 and 1,000 m on terraces.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to golden straw; fruity; slightly acid, harmonious. Reds: violet to garnet; fruity. Rosés: pale to deep pink; fruity, slightly acid, harmonious.

styles.name: Dulce clásico
styles.text: Whites amber and unctuous, reds reddish; raisined fruit, spice; velvety, intense.

styles.name: Vino de licor
styles.text: Golden to amber; intense aromas of raisined fruit and spice; velvety, intense.

styles.name: Vino espumoso
styles.text: Pale yellow to gold, fine persistent bubbles; intense, clean, fruity.
